mcqs.question: Under the India–US trade deal, what reciprocal tariff will the United States impose on Indian goods?
mcqs.explanation: The reciprocal US tariff on Indian goods was reduced from 25% to 18%. The tempting figure of 25% was the earlier tariff rate before the deal.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the India–US trade deal is incorrect?
options: The additional 25% punitive duty imposed over Russian oil purchases was removed.
India has regained Generalised System of Preferences (GSP), which was withdrawn in 2019.
India is expected to make purchases of up to USD 500 billion of US energy, agriculture, coal and technology.
Mission 500 aims to raise bilateral trade to USD 500 billion by 2030.
mcqs.explanation: India has not regained GSP; it was withdrawn in 2019. The other statements correctly describe the removal of the additional 25% duty, expected purchases of up to USD 500 billion, and the Mission 500 target of USD 500 billion by 2030.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the market-access provisions of the India–US Bilateral Trade Agreement, consider the following statements:
1. India will receive preferential access to the USD 30-trillion US market.
2. An 18% rate will apply to USD 900 billion of US imports.
3. Zero duty will apply to USD 180 billion of US imports.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the agreement provides preferential access to a USD 30-trillion US market and an 18% rate on USD 900 billion of US imports. Statement 3 is incorrect because the zero-duty provision covers USD 150 billion, not USD 180 billion.
